episodes.205340: An early September moisture surge resulted in the return of a more active weather pattern to Utah, including some isolated instances of flash flooding as well as a strong thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.205393: Seabreeze thunderstorms in SC stayed sub-severe over land but led to a severe marine wind gust.
episodes.205398: A weak disturbance rotating southeast around a ridge of high pressure over the Desert Southwest combined with higher moisture along and east of the central mountain chain resulting in the development of isolated strong to severe storms along the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. One of these storms produced nickel size hail at Ojo Feliz in Mora County. Isolated thunderstorms across eastern New Mexico quickly dissipated during the evening hours around sunset due to the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.205407: The atmosphere on September 7th remained well saturated, with PWAT values into the 1.9 to 2.2 inch range. This deep moisture combined with the passage of a frontal boundary that extended along the coast and continued to move offshore during the early morning hours produced periods of heavy rainfall across South Texas. This was particularly true along the Rio Grande. As the day progressed, moisture convergence, daytime heating, and subtle impulses of energy embedded in the northwest flow aloft were enough to support training thunderstorms across the Victoria Crossroads, leading to isolated flash flooding.
episodes.206315: A disturbance passing through brought scattered showers and thunderstorms across Southwest MT. Even through there were low amounts of instability, dry thunderstorms and deep mixing produced gusty winds with the strongest storms.
episodes.206503: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours along a cold front and near a weak area of low pressure. These storms moved slowly across the Charleston metro area through the mid afternoon and produced very heavy rainfall. The excessive rainfall resulted in numerous instances of flash flooding across the Charleston peninsula as well as in the West Ashley area. Observed rainfall amounts from CoCoRaHS observers and automated rain gages ranged from 1.5-4.0 inches for the entire event, including observed hourly rainfall rates of 2-3 inches.
episodes.206507: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front and near a weak area of low pressure in the mid afternoon hours. These storms moved across Chatham County and produced strong wind gusts and a few downed trees.
episodes.206632: A front approached from the northwest with a moist and unstable airmass ahead of it across the local area. Slow steering flow and high moisture across the area ahead of the front produced sea breeze showers and storms that produced locally heavy rainfall. Weak shear but high instability across the local marine waters produced waterspouts.

episodes.207572: Tropical moisture associated with a tropical wave and other trade wind perturbations, along with an upper-level trough resulted in the formation of strong showers and thunderstorms. These showers resulted in flooding, landslide and wind damage along portions of eastern, northern and western Puerto Rico.
episodes.207624: Isentropic lift over a relatively cool airmass produced showers and thunderstorms that eventually produced excessive rainfall and isolated flash flooding.

Additionally, the thunderstorm winds caused multiple power poles to be downed causing a power outage on the west side of the Tucson Metro.

A brief tornado touchdown occurred in Palm Bay as confirmed by a combination of photographic and video evidence from the public, as well as data from the National Weather Service Melbourne (KMLB) radar. KMLB radar indicates that at approximately 2:30 PM EDT, multiple thunderstorm boundary collisions led to the brief development of a circulation in south Palm Bay. Photos and videos shared via social media indicate the circulation likely touched down near Merrimac St SE and Cherokee Rd SE at approximately 2:36 PM EDT, before moving north along Airoso Rd SE for approximately 3 minutes. Minor damage was noted with some vegetative debris, mainly in the|form of broken tree branches and a small downed oak tree. Structural damage was confined to a few broken fence panels, twisted awnings, and a shed that was uplifted. Two homes in the vicinity of Airoso Rd SE and Cherokee Rd SE experienced minor roof|damage when some of their shingles were removed. This damage is coincident with an EF-0 tornado, with peak wind gusts of up to 65 mph. ||There are no known direct injuries or fatalities as a result of |the tornado.
